contributions.detail: exact (44 rows sum 22837.63 = stated 22,837.63 = Summary lines 1 and 4). p5 carries 39 rows summing 20662.63 and p6 carries 5 rows summing 2175.00

expenditures.detail: DELTA of -118,217.85 against stated, and the CAUSE is a per-filer semantic on the form itself, not a transcription gap. The itemized rows reconcile PERFECTLY to Schedule B's own arithmetic: p3 14 rows = 37,811.73 = its printed subtotal, p4 7 rows = 4,929.15 = its printed subtotal, and 37,811.73 + 4,929.15 = 42,740.88 = the printed TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE, which is also Summary LINE 6. The stated figure taken from Summary line 2 Column A is 160,958.73, a CUMULATIVE campaign-to-date number this filer put in Column A (the known Gill-2007 Column-A semantic); the balance chain proves line 6 is the period figure: line 3 20,949.04 + line 4 22,837.63 = line 5 43,786.67, and 43,786.67 - 42,740.88 = 1,045.79 = line 7. Nothing was recomputed or reconciled - both figures are retained verbatim

itemized.page_subtotal_gates: p3 (Schedule B) 14 rows sum 37,811.73 = printed SUBTOTAL FOR THIS PAGE 37,811.73 GATE PASS - and the gate ADJUDICATED row 12, whose hundreds digit is an over-inked blob (3,100.00, not 3,400.00). p4 (Schedule B) 7 rows sum 4,929.15 = printed subtotal 4,929.15 GATE PASS. p3+p4 = 42,740.88 = printed TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE GATE PASS. Schedule A is a spreadsheet attachment with NO subtotal or total line of its own, so no page-subtotal gate exists there; the gate used is the Summary Page (44 rows = 22,837.63 = lines 1 and 4), which PASSES exactly - p6's five rows come to exactly the 2,175.00 residual left by p5's 39.

itemized.notes: Sim Gill, District Attorney, Year-End Report January 31 (form checks 'January 31 of each year'; signed 1/31/07, clerk stamp JAN 31 2007). Schedule B is the county form on PDF pages 3 and 4 (the filer's own page numbers 3 of 4 and 4 of 4); Schedule A is a typed LANDSCAPE spreadsheet export on PDF pages 5-6, which needed a CLOCKWISE rotation to read - note that the other rotated attachment in this chunk (rhoruchi_09_YearEnd) needed the opposite sign, so the sign is per file. THE HEADLINE FINDING is the Column-A semantic: Summary line 2 (Total Expenditures Made, Column A) prints 160,958.73 while line 6 - and Schedule B's own printed total - print 42,740.88. This is the documented Gill-2007 case of a CUMULATIVE figure placed in Column A; the itemized side matches the period figure exactly, and both numbers are retained verbatim without reconciliation. The Schedule A spreadsheet prints Address 1 / City / St / Zip columns that are EMPTY on all 44 rows (the export carried no address data - not a redaction), so no donor geography exists in this filing; it also carries Occupation and Employer columns, preserved per row in the notes, and it CLIPS long Last Name values at the column edge. Two cells resisted every escalation and are handled honestly: Schedule B p3 row 1's recipient is left BLANK rather than guessed, and p4 row 2's recipient is kept as the literal partly-legible glyph string.
